subject: Run-rate variance & commit scenarios — renewal decision prep
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightcart.com>, Alex Turner <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Run-rate variance & commit scenarios — renewal decision prep

Hi Maria / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the call last week. My team pulled together a short run-rate diagnostic and three lightweight commit scenarios to help the BrightCart leadership and finance teams decide on renewal/expansion options. High-level signal: your three-month rolling token run-rate is ~37% above the existing committed baseline and your peak daily 99th-percentile latency has tightened by ~20ms since July, so performance is stable.

I've attached a CSV with per-route token spend and a short workbook that models the scenarios. Quick summary here:
- Current committed baseline: 12M tokens / month
- Trailing 3-month run-rate: ~16.4M tokens / month (37% uplift)
- Unit economics: host price ~ $3.40 per 1M tokens; after potential commit discount ranges project net price down to $2.60–$3.00 per 1M depending on tier and term.

Options we think are worth considering (details in commit_scenarios_v3.xlsx):
1) Option A — 12-month renewal, 15% uplift to 13.8M tokens/mo, modest 8% discount, predictable billing cadence.
2) Option B — 18-month commitment, 25% uplift to 15M tokens/mo, deeper 17% discount + priority burst capacity (recommended if you expect sustained growth).
3) Option C — Dynamic commit (quarterly true-up) with baseline increase to 14M tokens/mo and no term extension — offers flexibility but fewer unit-cost savings.

Action items for BrightCart: quick read of the workbook, tell us which option you want modeled with your tax & billing constraints. If useful, I can loop in Ben from finance for exact pricing and Jordan for any SLA or dedicated capacity questions.

Thanks — aiming to get pressure-tested numbers for your renewal decision by next Friday.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments (3): brightcart_q3_usage_by_route.csv, latency_dashboard_oct.png, commit_scenarios_v3.xlsx
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightcart.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Run-rate variance & commit scenarios — renewal decision prep

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. A couple of immediate clarifying questions from our side:

1) The run-rate includes a recent feature rollout (personalized search) that drove a one-time spike — are the numbers normalized to exclude the initial heavy indexing day?
2) We need the model to show cash flow impact by quarter (not just annualized savings) because our CFO wants to see quarter-by-quarter P&L.

Also curious on the latency note — our infra team measured a few 500ms outliers on two dates last month (should be in the CSV). Can Jordan comment on root cause / mitigation (we're sensitive to tail latency for checkout flows).

Goal: present a preferred option to our CFO by 10/31. Can you get updated numbers by end of week?

— Maria
VP Product, BrightCart
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightcart.com>, Alex Turner <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Run-rate variance & commit scenarios — renewal decision prep

Great questions, Maria — short answers and next steps below.

1) Normalization: the attached CSV contains a column 'spike_flag' and I removed the single-day indexing spike from the run-rate numbers in the workbook. The trailing 3-month run-rate number I quoted earlier is normalized.

2) Cash flow by quarter: Ben (cc'd) will add a Q-by-Q cash flow sheet to the workbook showing invoicing and net cash impact for each commit tier. Ben — can you add a quarterly view and model timing of discounts vs invoice recognition?

Latency tail: Jordan, can you look at the two 500ms outliers in the latency_dashboard_oct.png and add a one-paragraph note for Maria on likely cause and mitigations (KV cache, batching thresholds, or cold-starts)?

Proposed timeline: we'll send an updated workbook with quarter cash flows, a short ROI slide (3 bullets) and a brief mitigation note by 10/28 EOD so you can review before the 10/31 CFO meeting.

If that works I will prepare a simplified two-column proposal (Option B preferred + fallback Option C) and Ben will enumerate the exact price ladder.

Thanks — talk soon.
Soojin
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Run-rate variance & commit scenarios — renewal decision prep

Hi team — attached is the updated commit_scenarios_v3.xlsx with a new 'Quarterly Cash Flow' tab and three clear pricing ladders tied to the options Soojin outlined. Key notes:
- Option A (12mo / 15% uplift): effective net $2.98 per 1M tokens. Quarterly savings vs current plan: Q1 2.5%, Q2 5.1%, Q3 7.8%, Q4 8.6% (reflects seasonality).
- Option B (18mo / 25% uplift + priority burst): effective net $2.65 per 1M tokens. Quarterly smoothing gives larger upfront invoice in Q1, then lower average unit cost across term.
- Option C (flex true-up): no term discount; we show a conservative cash-flow model for constrained CFO appetite.

I've also added a short clause we can include for a one-time true-up credit if BrightCart exceeds 200% of the committed monthly run-rate in a single quarter (protects against surprise spikes).

If Maria confirms preferred option by EOD 10/30 we can issue an updated MPA and optional DocuSign routing.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Finance
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Alex Turner <alex@brightcart.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Run-rate variance & commit scenarios — renewal decision prep

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team. After a fast internal sync with Maria and finance, BrightCart is inclined to move forward with Option B (18-month, 25% uplift + priority burst). We want the DocuSign-ready MPA with the quarterly cash-flow schedule Benjamin prepared and the 200% spike credit clause included.

Two asks before we sign:
1) Please add an explicit SLA line item for burst capacity availability during Black Friday week (we can accept an availability target + brief remediation credit).
2) Share the updated latency mitigation note Jordan mentioned so our infra lead can thumbs-up it.

If we get those in an updated MPA by EOD 11/02, we can route for signatures the same day.

Thanks — Alex
Head of Engineering, BrightCart
